ref.title: Old drugs and New challenges: A narrative review of nitazenes

sources.title: Old Drugs and New Challenges: A Narrative Review of Nitazenes

design.quote: This is a narrative review that used the PubMed and Google Scholar databases to search for peer-reviewed articles on nitazenes. The authors also consulted authoritative websites such as those run by the DEA, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and government-run websites for late-breaking information on these agents.
design.text: Narrative review of nitazenes using literature and authoritative sources

findings.quote: Nitazenes are available in powders, counterfeit tablets, or liquids and may be mixed with inert substances and/or combined with other drugs, such as heroin, fentanyl, and benzodiazepines. Their inclusion in other drug products is not detectable by consumers and may not be disclosed to them by sellers.
findings.text: Nitazenes are often mixed with other drugs and are not detectable by consumers.

findings.quote: In theory, some nitazenes can be antagonized by the opioid receptor antagonists, such as naloxone and nalmefene, but it is not clear if the high potency and impurities of the nitazenes might limit the effectiveness of the available antagonists.
findings.text: Naloxone and nalmefene may not effectively reverse nitazene overdose due to high potency and impurities.

findings.quote: Certain nitazenes can be more potent than fentanyl and are increasingly found on the illicit drug market in North America and Europe. These agents may not be disclosed to buyers of illicit drugs and are often mixed with fentanyl or other agents. They are associated with morbidity and mortality, and it is not known how effective naloxone or other antagonists are when reversing nitazene-induced respiratory depression.
findings.text: Nitazenes are associated with morbidity and mortality, and the effectiveness of naloxone in reversing their respiratory depression is unknown.

limits.quote: The lethal doses for nitazenes in humans, particularly in combination with other drugs or medical conditions, are not known.
limits.text: The lethal dose of nitazenes in humans is not known.
